body:
`scripts/findings.py` writes one JSON per finding (merge-safe, as designed) but
ALSO regenerates `findings/INDEX.md`, a single file listing every finding, and
that file is committed. Two findings branches cut from the same main therefore
rewrite the same lines of INDEX.md and the second one to be reviewed goes
CONFLICTING.

OBSERVED 2026-08-07: PR #1423 (`findings/INDEX.md` + `findings/items/F-123292.json`)
sits `mergeable=CONFLICTING, mergeStateStatus=DIRTY` with auto-merge armed. It is
green on every required check. The conflict is the blocker — not, as a previous
tick's note concluded, the tier-1 path regex (which enforces nothing; see the
sibling finding).

This defeats the module docstring's own promise: "Storage is one JSON file per
finding under findings/items/, which makes concurrent branches merge without
conflicts." The per-item storage does. The index re-introduces exactly the
contention it avoids, and the autopilot files findings from several branches, so
it hits this routinely.

Options, cheapest first:
  * stop committing INDEX.md — regenerate on demand (`findings.py index`) and
    gitignore it; nothing reads it programmatically;
  * keep it committed but add a `.gitattributes` merge driver that regenerates
    it on conflict;
  * generate it in CI on merge to main rather than in the contributing branch.

Prefer the first: an index derived from files already in the tree is not source.
title: findings/INDEX.md is generated and committed, so concurrent findings PRs always conflict
